extracted.intended_audience: journal editors and editorial staff (editors, associate editors, managing editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal editors on overseeing the full peer review workflow: initial checks, selecting and retaining reviewers, handling ethics (conflicts, co-authorship), using submission systems, and recognising reviewer contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor initial checks and suitability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript good enough for peer review? Does it conform to Aims & Scope, style guidelines, and Instructions for Authors? Does it make a significant contribution to the existing literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors carry out initial checks before sending manuscripts to review and may reject unsuitable manuscripts without peer review at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning manuscripts and editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign the manuscript to the right associate editor, find appropriate reviewers, and ensure ethical integrity during the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors oversee the peer review process from start to finish and are responsible for recommending a decision based on reviewer reports and communicating that decision to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation and communication of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: After peer review, the editor will recommend a decision based on the reports they receive and inform the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may revise the paper until it’s suitable for publication; editors manage subsequent rounds and final acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectations about time and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review involves many people and intricate steps; it is generally the slowest part of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the multiple roles (editor, associate editors, admin, reviewers, editorial systems team, managing editor) and steps (initial checks, assigning, finding reviewers, ethical checks, writing reviews) helps editors manage timelines and set realistic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-requesting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s best not to request more reviews than required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting extra reviews may decrease review times but risks overburdening the finite pool of reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate delays: difficulty finding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty in finding appropriate reviewers is a common source of delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grow and strengthen the reviewer pool via systems and editorial board engagement to mitigate this delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate delays: delayed reviewer responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Delayed response from reviewers can slow the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reminders (automatic or personal emails) and ask reviewers if they are still able to provide a report or to recommend alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate delays: unhelpful review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Unhelpful reviews (e.g., a single sentence or paragraph) impede editorial decisions and author revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A normal review report should be two to three pages in length, sometimes longer; encourage substantive, constructive reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reminding reviewers and eliciting responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Send automatic reminders or personal emails to prompt reviewers, remind them of the importance of their report, and check availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they cannot review, ask them to recommend someone else; reminding that the editor can reassign the review may provoke a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using peer review systems to build reviewer pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use submission/peer review systems and the editorial board to grow and strengthen your pool of potential reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage features of ScholarOne/Editorial Manager and other tools to find and manage reviewers efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set predefined keywords for reviewer matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keywords/classifications to find peer reviewers; authors often submit their own keywords which editorial teams use to locate suitable reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing pre-defined keywords consider ensuring the list is as extensive as possible and decide whether it should be a compulsory submission field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save search preferences in reviewer selection tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Set and save search preferences (e.g., within ScholarOne's 'Set my search preferences') to make future reviewer searches efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predetermine how you want search results to appear so selection is quicker and more consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer-selection metrics displayed in systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Default search results may display the number of review assignments in the past 12 months, days since last review, and average R-score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these displayed metrics to inform reviewer selection and avoid overburdened or inactive reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer locator/discovery tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated tools (Reviewer Locator on ScholarOne; Reviewer Discovery on Editorial Manager) that match manuscripts to reviewers based on keywords, abstract, title, or external profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools draw from extensive databases and ProQuest scholar profiles to make finding reviewers easier and faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly assess and maintain the reviewer list
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly check reviewer lists to prevent them becoming outdated and to ensure they contain willing, reliable reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run performance reports once or twice a year to identify best reviewers for rewards and weed out non-responders; expire reviewer roles when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thanking reviewers and keeping their data current
rubrics_metrics.description: Send thank you letters after report completion and prompt reviewers to update their details and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate, updated keywords and contact details keep keyword-matching tools effective and encourage reviewer retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage the editorial board as reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the editorial board for feedback, filtering inappropriate papers, reviewing based on specialism, and recruiting reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add topics/keywords to board member profiles, invite them to review, encourage recruitment at conferences, and engage early-career researchers to increase reviewer diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewer support and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Support reviewers with guidance and recognition to retain them and encourage quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer reviewer guidelines, certificates of recognition, 30-days free access to journal content, annual 'thanks to reviewers' lists, book discounts, and integration with Publons for tracking and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for reviewer bias and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Select reviewers who are experts but check for conflicts of interest (recent collaborators, shared affiliations) that may bias reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably a reviewer should not have worked with the author in the last three years; reviewers must declare conflicts before agreeing; if conflicts exist assign alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage author-suggested and excluded reviewers cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest or exclude reviewers, but suggested reviewers pose a risk of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are recommended to select their own reviewers; Taylor & Francis removed the 'Preferred Reviewers' function from ScholarOne and Editorial Manager to minimise this risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-author verification at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-check validity of all co-authors’ contact details at submission and ensure all co-authors consent to being named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Corresponding Author is responsible for co-author consent; checking co-author details prevents delays and educates inexperienced authors on correct practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable and act on co-author notification features
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ScholarOne’s feature that sends an email alert to each listed co-author when a manuscript is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notifies co-authors that a paper has been submitted in their name and allows those named without approval to respond; enable this feature where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle invalid co-author contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: If co-author email addresses are incorrect or bounce, request current valid institutional email addresses from the submitting author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If co-author emails bounce, ask the submitting author for updated contact details to ensure co-authors are properly notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit papers to correct incomplete/incorrect co-author lists
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission form lists only the submitting author but the manuscript lists additional names, unsubmit the paper and return it to the corresponding author for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting preserves the submission form and files under 'Unsubmitted Manuscripts' and is not the same as rejection; explain reasons and steps required in the accompanying email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for checking co-author details in ScholarOne
rubrics_metrics.description: Step-by-step actions: if co-authors missing, click 'Manuscript Files' to unsubmit and email the corresponding author explaining corrections; if contact details incorrect, request correct details; for author list changes, require cover letter explaining changes and written confirmations from co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record all correspondence in the Audit Trail in ScholarOne and follow COPE resources/guidelines when misconduct or disputes are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to COPE resources for complex ethical guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines for issues such as sharing information on possible misconduct, text recycling, ethical editing, and consent for publishing medical case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE materials provide additional, detailed ethical guidelines editors should consult when handling misconduct or complicated authorship/ethics issues.
